title: Find the evidence first, then explain
statement: For an answer that needs evidence, have the learner first find and mark the evidence in the text, then explain it in their own words in a separate slot.
detail: Reviews of a Grade 3 reading course flagged its evidence-writing task as backwards in two consecutive rounds, on 2026-07-20 and 2026-07-24: finding and copying the sentence and then rewording it in one box teaches plagiarism (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/feedback/feedback3/FEEDBACK_RESPONSE.md`, item 9; `grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g3-reading/FEEDBACK-LEDGER.md`). The fix asked for was to highlight or underline the sentence in the text first and then write in the learner's own words, or to split the task into two parts. Keep the source in view while the learner does this, and let the evidence come from more than one place if need be. The quote then holds only the text's words, and the inference has to be produced, not copied.

evidence.quote: **The writing task teaches plagiarism**: find-and-copy-the-sentence then own-words in one box.
Highlight/underline in the text first, then write in own words; or split into two parts.
Reverse to **find-and-highlight the sentence FIRST, then write it in your own words**;
Prompts ask for textual evidence, but the passage is hidden when the student needs to cite it.
No model of a strong response is shown.
The current order is backwards. Students should first find and highlight the sentence, then write it in their own words: find it, then write about it. The I-do should model the evidence-finding step.
"say it with evidence" had write-then-find; correct is find+highlight FIRST, then write in own words
often it's 2 ideas synthesized from different places
copy-then-paraphrase writing prompts that teach plagiarism (fix: highlight the sentence IN the text, then write in own words — or split into two explicit parts)
Evidence tasks: find-and-highlight the sentence first, then write in own words; the I-do models the finding
